title: Officer who investigated Surrey's A3 'ghost crash' gives exclusive interview
excerpt: An officer who investigated the crash has shared his recollections with Surrey Live
content:
Officer who investigated Surrey's famous A3 'ghost crash' gives exclusive interview more than 20 years on

An officer who investigated the crash has shared his recollections with Surrey Live

07:00, 31 Oct 2026

New details have been shared by those who experienced possibly Surrey’s most ‘paranormal’ event in recent memory.

‌

‌

The A3 ‘ghost crash’ lives on as one of the most puzzling incidents to have taken place in Guildford this side of the 21st Century.

‌

Speculation about what took place that day has spread as far as the United States, with various podcasts and documentaries attempting to work out what happened on the A3 that December evening almost 25 years ago.

‌

There are not many people who can offer a first-hand account of what they saw on December 11, 2002. One person who can is Keith Brown, a now retired coroner’s officer who was called to the scene after police located the crashed vehicle.

Mr Brown has shared his recollections of the so-called A3 ‘ghost crash’ in an exclusive interview with SurreyLive.

A ‘ghost crash’ on the A3?

First, it is important to establish what led this incident to be associated with paranormal activity.

‌

According to Surrey Police ’s statement issued at the time, on the evening of December 11, 2002, officers received multiple reports from drivers that they had witnessed a car lose control and fly off the A3 not long before the slip road at Burpham, Guildford.

Officers who attended the scene attempted to locate this crashed vehicle, but are said to have initially found no evidence of an incident at the location it had been reported.

‌

It was not until officers completed searches of the wider area that they discovered a crashed Vauxhall Astra, which was nose down in a ditch. A few meters away from the car were the skeletal remains of a man.

‌

This body was later identified as Christopher Brian Chandler, a 20-year-old who had been wanted by the Metropolitan Police since July that year.

Chandler is thought to have crashed on the A3 up to five months before his body was found.

‌

A media frenzy ensued after news came out about the incident. Many speculated what drivers witnessed that evening which led them to report seeing a crash on the motorway; with some going as far as to suggest people were seeing a ‘paranormal replay’ of Chandler’s crash months prior.

Surrey Police insisted that the incident would be treated as a regular road collision. An inquest into Chandler’s death was held in August 2003, where it was determined that it would be impossible to truly ascertain how the 20-year-old had died, largely due to how long it had been before the crash was discovered.

‌

Keith Brown was among the officials to have worked on the case. Serving as a coroner’s officer at the time, he was tasked with investigating the incident on behalf of the HM Coroner Court for Surrey, and handing his findings over.

The inquest into Christopher Chandler was held at the HM Coroner Court in Woking in August 2003. Coroner Dr Karin Chandler concluded the inquest with an open verdict.

‌

An officer’s recollections

Almost 25 years later, Keith Brown spoke with SurreyLive to share his first-hand account of what he saw that evening on December 11, 2002, and his thoughts on what came after.

“I was on call as the coroner's officer for the area, and got a call that evening advising me that there had been a road traffic collision on the A3 and someone had been found deceased.

‌

“I don't know how many calls came in, some people say loads, others only a couple. All I know is that someone had reported that they'd seen an accident.

“I had parked on an escape road nearby and walked to the scene to meet with police. I knew the traffic officers who had made it to the scene first very well.

‌

“They were both very experienced and my understanding is that they were using a torch to locate the crash site at the site reported, but there was nothing obvious on the motorway. As they were looking further up, they saw a reflection of a car in their torches.

‌

“As they made their way through the undergrowth and found a vehicle; it had obviously been there for some time. No one was in the vehicle. The remains of the driver were found a few meters away, at that point it was a skeleton.

“I came along with an accident investigation officer, but it was decided that because it was too dark to investigate the scene. We returned the next morning to collect the evidence and the corpse was later transported to the Royal Surrey Hospital for analysis.”

‌

As a coroner’s officer, Mr Brown was tasked with presenting evidence of the crash to HM Coroner for Surrey as part of an inquest into Chandler’s death.

Reflecting on this, Keith continued: “It appeared that the vehicle had flown off the road because of the way it seemed to have landed. But there was no evidence to indicate how he had crashed.

‌

“My recollection is that he (Chandler) was heading down the A3 because he had friends in the area. It was probably late at night when it happened.

“I think he’d been drinking with friends, but he had left them. Nobody had seen him after that and nobody had reported an incident occurring at the time he is believed to have been heading down A3.

‌

“He had been quite seriously injured but had managed to get out of the vehicle. He didn’t make much progress before he unfortunately died.

‌

“One of the things officers believe may have happened is that when he lost control of the vehicle and the car left the road; it passed through the thick bushes, which then flung back; essentially covering the crash site. This happened in Summer time, so by December some of the foliage had thinned out.”

“Everything is all conjecture. All we can say is that the vehicle obviously left the road, but we don’t know why. There was nothing at the time which indicated there had been an incident.

‌

“Because of the length of time it took for him to be found, we can’t determine whether he had a mental episode, whether there was a fault with the vehicle, or an obstruction on the road.

“I have dealt with hundreds of deaths, but there are ones which I will always remember. This is one of those. It was unusual to find skeletal remains at a scene, the crash had obviously happened months before.”

‌

The retired coroner’s officer then spoke on the ‘paranormal’ speculation which has surrounded this incident in the decades since.

“I have seen a lot of things over the subsequent years about the crash, I would say a lot of it is factually incorrect. One of the biggest things is that they say the body wasn’t actually found on the evening, it was found on the following day. Some say the body was found in the vehicle, it wasn’t.

‌

“It could have been a coincidence and some drivers did actually see something happen (on the evening of December 11, 2002). There is a lot of speculation that has come out about this incident.

“I’ve spent my whole working life dealing with factual things. As a coroner's officer, presenting facts to the coroner is all we can do.

“Judgements have to be based on the facts we find, and if people want to look at those facts and make something different out of them, that is entirely their choice.”
